title: Docs: internal runbooks + oncall playbook updates for Dedicated staged rollouts (pause/rollback)
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Goal
Create operator-facing runbooks and update the oncall playbook to safely operate Dedicated staged rollouts in reserved GPU pools, with a focus on pause/hold conditions, rollback/abort, and incident response. This work is needed before enabling beta customers and before GA.

Context
Dedicated pools have strict isolation and limited headroom; a bad model/runtime/config rollout can saturate the pool and violate Dedicated SLAs. The new staged rollout system introduces gates (latency, 5xx, timeouts, GPU utilization, queue depth) and automatic hold behavior when thresholds fail or when metrics are missing/late. Oncall needs clear, deterministic steps to:
- identify why a rollout paused/held
- decide proceed vs rollback/abort
- verify metric freshness and evaluator health
- communicate status internally + to enterprise customers
- capture audit trail expectations

Scope / Deliverables
1) Publish and/or update the following Confluence pages:
- Runbook: Dedicated staged rollout paused/held
- Runbook: Rollback/abort a Dedicated staged rollout safely
- Oncall playbook updates: Dedicated rollouts section (triage signals, dashboards, escalation paths)
- "Known failure modes" section (metrics missing, evaluator lag, routing weight stuck, approval race)

2) Include concrete links and commands for operators (CLI/admin tooling), including:
- how to fetch rollout status + gate evaluation summaries
- how to confirm evaluator health and query freshness
- how to abort/rollback and confirm traffic weights converge
- where to find audit events (approve/abort/auto-hold)

3) Align with SRE and Security on:
- pause vs rollback guidance (what triggers immediate rollback)
- approval requirements during incident conditions
- audit log fields required for compliance-oriented customers

Non-goals
- Customer-facing documentation (handled separately as part of beta/GA release notes)
- Writing a full postmortem template (we will link to the standard incident process)

Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Confluence runbook for paused/held rollouts contains a step-by-step triage flow with decision points and "stop-the-line" guidance.
- [ ] Confluence runbook for rollback/abort includes pre-checks (headroom, autoscaling guardrails), explicit commands, and post-checks (routing weights, queue depth recovery).
- [ ] Oncall playbook includes dedicated-rollouts-specific symptoms, dashboards, alert names, and escalation owners (Platform/SRE/Infra/Security/CS).
- [ ] Runbooks reference the correct dashboards/alerts (gate evaluator health + per-pool rollout status).
- [ ] Runbooks include comms templates (internal incident channel + customer update stub) and who to page.
- [ ] Reviewed/approved by Sean Gallagher (SRE) and Chloe Martin (Console backend) for operational correctness.

Proposed Runbook Structure (outline)
A) Runbook: "Dedicated staged rollout is Paused/Held"
- Entry criteria: rollout state == HOLD/PAUSED, or stage advancement stalled > N minutes
- Quick severity classification:
  - Sev2: p95 latency breach for tenant, queue depth rising, error rate > threshold
  - Sev3: rollout paused but tenant SLOs ok
- Step 1: Confirm current state
  - Identify tenant_id, pool_id, rollout_plan_id, plan_version, stage_id
  - Confirm which stage is active and the intended next stage
- Step 2: Identify hold reason
  - Gate failure (latency/5xx/timeouts/utilization/queue)
  - Missing/late metrics (fail-safe hold)
  - Evaluator degraded (global hold policy)
  - Approval required (manual gate)
  - Policy/routing mismatch (weights not applied)
- Step 3: Validate signal quality
  - Check evaluator lag dashboard and metrics freshness
  - Confirm cardinality/label issues aren’t hiding data
  - Cross-check with pool-level metrics (queue depth/utilization) independent of gate summaries
- Step 4: Decide action
  - Proceed (manual approve) only if:
    - metrics are fresh, evaluator healthy
    - failing metric is explained and resolved (e.g., transient load)
    - pool headroom is sufficient
  - Rollback/abort if:
    - tenant is in active incident or approaching SLO breach
    - utilization/queue depth indicates saturation risk
    - repeated gate failures across evaluation windows
    - evaluator is unreliable and we can’t trust gate outcomes
- Step 5: Communicate
  - Post status in #incidents / #eng-platform as appropriate
  - Engage CS (Rachel Kim/Miguel Santos) if customer-impacting
- Step 6: Document
  - Link to audit events for approval/abort
  - Capture timestamps, stage, and gating metrics in incident notes

B) Runbook: "Rollback/Abort Dedicated staged rollout"
- Preconditions:
  - Confirm target is rollback to previous stable plan_version (or abort to 0% new version)
  - Verify autoscaling guardrails and minimum headroom policy status
  - Confirm if rollback requires additional approvals (incident override path)
- Execution:
  - Abort rollout (preferred) vs rollback to prior plan_version (if supported by tooling)
  - Verify routing weights converge deterministically and no partial stage remains
  - Confirm data plane configs updated across pool
- Post-checks:
  - Monitor queue depth + utilization for recovery
  - Verify error rate and latency return to baseline within N minutes
  - Ensure rollout is marked aborted with actor + reason

Oncall Playbook Updates (specific adds)
- New section: "Dedicated staged rollouts"
  - Primary alerts to watch:
    - Gate evaluator lag / failed evaluations
    - Paused rollouts count > threshold
    - Rollout stuck-in-stage > threshold
    - Dedicated pool queue depth high during rollout
  - Primary dashboards:
    - Dedicated Rollouts: per-pool status
    - Gate evaluation health (success rate, metrics latency)
    - Dedicated pool saturation (queue depth, GPU util)
  - Escalation:
    - Platform oncall (control plane / evaluator)
    - Infra oncall (fleet/autoscaling guardrails)
    - SRE oncall (SLO impact + comms)
    - Security (audit log export issues only)
- Add "Known failure modes" quick reference:
  - Missing metrics -> fail-safe HOLD (common in staging; should be rare in prod)
  - Evaluator lag -> global hold; treat as incident if customer rollouts blocked
  - Approval race condition -> verify plan_version + stage event stream
  - Weight application drift -> verify routing service has latest policy version

  - Approvals + audit logging: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-028-rollout-approvals-and-audit-logging.json

Reviewers
- Sean Gallagher (SRE): operational correctness, escalation, thresholds language
- Allison Grant (Observability): dashboards/alerts names and links
- Chloe Martin (Console backend): workflow alignment with actual UI/status
- Marcus Lin (Security): audit references are accurate (no promises beyond retention/export)

Open questions
- Do we want a default "incident override" approval path (e.g., SRE oncall can abort without Dedicated operator role)? If yes, document and link to RBAC policy.
- For missing metrics holds: do we recommend rollback by default, or allow a short grace period? (Need final guidance from SRE + PM-420 defaults)

Implementation notes
This ticket is docs-only but depends on the final alert names + evaluator behavior. If alert naming or dashboard URLs change during beta, update links in Confluence before GA.
